relevance_to_phd: Catalyzes AI capabilities applied to remote sensing and analysis.

name: AlphaGo vs Lee Sedol
description: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol; milestone in reinforcement learning and AI.
relevance_to_phd: Signals practical advances in AI relevant across analysis tasks.

name: Attention Is All You Need
description: Research paper introducing the Transformer architecture; foundational for modern AI models.
relevance_to_phd: Shapes AI used for classification, analysis, and infrastructure orchestration.

name: China REE Export Restrictions
description: China restricts rare earth element exports; exposes material dependencies in tech supply chains.
relevance_to_phd: Highlights material underpinnings of sensors, electronics, and green tech infrastructures.

name: R.G. Collingwood
description: British philosopher-historian who developed re-enactment theory: historical understanding as re-thinking past actors' thoughts.
relevance_to_phd: Useful for analyzing technical reasoning in calibration and infrastructure decisions.

name: Carlo Ginzburg
description: Italian historian who pioneered microhistory and evidential paradigm analyzing traces and clues.
key_works: The Cheese and the Worms; Clues, Myths, and the Historical Method
relevance_to_phd: Supports close studies of calibration practices and sensor work.

name: Reinhart Koselleck
description: German historian who developed conceptual history (Begriffsgeschichte) analyzing semantic change over time.
relevance_to_phd: Frames changing meanings of 'calibration', 'precision', 'data quality'.

name: Natalie Zemon Davis
description: American-Canadian historian who advanced narrative microhistory and cultural history.
key_works: The Return of Martin Guerre; Fiction in the Archives
relevance_to_phd: Useful for technician-centered case narratives in infrastructures.

name: Herbert Butterfield
description: British historian who critiqued 'Whig interpretation' of history and teleological progress narratives.
relevance_to_phd: Guards against progress narratives in technology histories.

name: Benedetto Croce
description: Italian philosopher arguing all history is contemporary history shaped by present concerns.
key_works: Theory and History of Historiography; History as the Story of Liberty
relevance_to_phd: Supports reflexivity in telling infrastructure histories.

name: Paul Otlet
description: Belgian bibliographer who created the Mundaneum; developed universal classification and documentation systems.
relevance_to_phd: Precursor to information infrastructures and data organization.

name: Vannevar Bush
description: American engineer who proposed the Memex concept influencing hypertext and information retrieval.
relevance_to_phd: Frames digital information architecture underlying data infrastructures.

name: Claude Shannon
description: Founder of information theory establishing mathematical basis for digital communication.
relevance_to_phd: Underpins data transmission in sensor and satellite networks.

name: Norbert Wiener
description: Founder of cybernetics studying control and communication in machines and living beings.
relevance_to_phd: Relevant for feedback loops in automated monitoring and control.

name: Marshall McLuhan
description: Canadian media theorist analyzing how media technologies shape cognition and society.
relevance_to_phd: Helps read satellites and sensors as media extending perception.

name: Elizabeth Eisenstein
description: Historian of print culture analyzing the printing press as agent of change in early modern Europe.
key_works: The Printing Press as an Agent of Change
relevance_to_phd: Analogy for digital information infrastructures and transformation.

name: Ann Blair
description: Historian of early modern information management and note-taking practices.
relevance_to_phd: Historical analogs for managing large climate datasets.

name: Peter Burke
description: Cultural historian who wrote a social history of knowledge examining production and circulation.
relevance_to_phd: Useful for understanding knowledge production in infrastructures.

name: Lewis Mumford
description: Historian of technology analyzing relations among technology, culture, and civilization.
key_works: Technics and Civilization; The Myth of the Machine
relevance_to_phd: Critical context for infrastructure and power.

name: Thomas P. Hughes
description: Historian who developed systems approach to technology studying large technical systems.
relevance_to_phd: Directly applicable to satellite and sensor networks.

name: David Edgerton
description: Historian critiquing innovation-centric narratives emphasizing technology-in-use and maintenance.
relevance_to_phd: Centers maintenance over invention for sensor network upkeep.

name: Ruth Schwartz Cowan
description: Historian of household technology and women's work; shows how technology reorganizes labor.
relevance_to_phd: Analogous gendered labor issues in monitoring infrastructures.

name: Langdon Winner
description: Political theorist of technology arguing artifacts have politics.
key_works: The Whale and the Reactor; Autonomous Technology
relevance_to_phd: Design choices in sensors encode political decisions.

name: Carolyn Marvin
description: Communication scholar of early electrical communication technologies.
relevance_to_phd: Historical perspective on the 'newness' of satellite/sensor media.

name: Lorraine Daston
description: Historian who developed historical epistemology and analysis of objectivity and epistemic virtues.
key_works: Objectivity (with Galison); Wonders and the Order of Nature
relevance_to_phd: Essential for changing norms of precision and objectivity in measurement.

name: Peter Galison
description: Historian of physics/material culture; trading zones concept; co-authored Objectivity.
key_works: Image and Logic; Einstein's Clocks, Poincaré's Maps; Objectivity (with Daston)
key_contributions: Trading zones; material culture of physics.
relevance_to_phd: Frames coordination between field scientists and technicians.

name: Steven Shapin
description: Historian of science studying social dimensions of scientific knowledge and experiment.
key_works: Leviathan and the Air-Pump (with Schaffer); A Social History of Truth
relevance_to_phd: Direct relevance to calibration and data quality.

name: Simon Schaffer
description: Historian of science focusing on instruments and practices; co-authored Leviathan and the Air-Pump.
relevance_to_phd: Material culture of instruments aligns with sensors and calibration.

name: Ian Hacking
description: Philosopher of science on historical ontology and styles of reasoning.
key_works: Representing and Intervening; The Taming of Chance; The Emergence of Probability
relevance_to_phd: Clarifies emergence of measurement concepts and practices.

name: Robert K. Merton
description: Sociologist of science; developed norms/ethos of science and analyzed social structure of science.
key_works: The Sociology of Science; Science, Technology and Society in Seventeenth Century England
relevance_to_phd: Relevance to credit and recognition in measurement work.

name: Joseph Needham
description: Historian of Chinese science and technology; challenged Eurocentric narratives.
relevance_to_phd: Important for non-Western perspectives on infrastructures and science.

name: Sandra Harding
description: Philosopher who developed standpoint theory and postcolonial science analysis.
key_works: The Science Question in Feminism; Sciences from Below
relevance_to_phd: Centers marginalized perspectives in measurement systems.

name: Helen Longino
description: Philosopher of science developing feminist epistemology and contextual empiricism.
key_works: Science as Social Knowledge; The Fate of Knowledge
relevance_to_phd: Shows how social context shapes measurement practices.

name: Susan Leigh Star
description: Sociologist of science/information; concepts of invisible work, boundary objects, and infrastructure studies.
key_works: Sorting Things Out (with Bowker); Institutional Ecology...
relevance_to_phd: Core to labor visibility and articulation work in infrastructures.

name: Geoffrey C. Bowker
description: Information scholar on classification, memory, and infrastructure; co-authored 'Sorting Things Out'.
key_works: Sorting Things Out (with Star); Memory Practices in the Sciences
relevance_to_phd: Links classification systems to infrastructure operations and memory.

name: Karin Knorr-Cetina
description: Sociologist of science who developed the concept of epistemic cultures.
relevance_to_phd: Explains varied knowledge-making practices across labs and fields.

name: Maintenance Studies
description: Field studying repair, maintenance, and care work keeping infrastructures functioning.
relevance_to_phd: Essential for invisible labour in sensor networks and calibration facilities.

name: Sociology of Scientific Knowledge
description: Approach studying how social factors shape scientific knowledge production (Edinburgh/Bath schools).
relevance_to_phd: Foundational for social shaping of measurement knowledge.

name: Large Technical Systems
description: Approach analyzing complex sociotechnical systems (e.g., electricity, transport) as integrated systems.
relevance_to_phd: Applies directly to satellite systems and sensor networks.

name: Social Epistemology
description: Study of social dimensions of knowledge production and collective knowledge practices.
relevance_to_phd: Explains social processes behind acceptance of measurement data.

name: History of the Book
description: Field studying books as material and social artifacts: production, circulation, reading.
relevance_to_phd: Analogy for thinking datasets/archives as material artifacts.

name: Critical Infrastructure Studies
description: Interdisciplinary field examining power relations and politics embedded in infrastructures.
relevance_to_phd: Key for dissertation focus on power and maintenance.

name: Invisible Work
description: Concept (Susan Leigh Star) describing labor essential to systems yet unrecognized.
relevance_to_phd: Core for analyzing labour visibility in infrastructures.

name: Articulation Work
description: Concept (Anselm Strauss) for work coordinating and integrating distributed activities.
relevance_to_phd: Critical in distributed sensor networks and calibration workflows.

name: Epistemic Cultures
description: Concept (Knorr-Cetina) for knowledge-making cultures differing across scientific fields.
relevance_to_phd: Important for field vs lab practices in measurement.

name: Inscription Devices
description: Concept (Latour & Woolgar) for instruments transforming matter/signals into traces.
relevance_to_phd: Sensors/satellites transform environments into data.

name: Immutable Mobiles
description: Concept (Latour) describing objects stable and transportable, enabling action at a distance.
relevance_to_phd: Calibration standards as immutable mobiles across sites.

name: Styles of Reasoning
description: Concept (Ian Hacking) on historically emergent ways of establishing truth.
relevance_to_phd: Different styles in measurement science vs field practice.

name: The Mangle of Practice
description: Andrew Pickering's study of scientific practice emphasizing material agency and temporal emergence.
relevance_to_phd: Relevant for calibration as emergent practice.

name: The Golem
description: Harry Collins and Trevor Pinch's introduction to sociology of science showing science's flexibility.
relevance_to_phd: Helps frame measurement science as context-dependent.

name: Archives Power
description: Randall Jimerson's critical examination of archives' role in shaping memory and power.
relevance_to_phd: Politics of data archives relevant to climate data repositories.

name: Founding of Royal Society
description: Founding of the Royal Society of London; institutionalizing experimental philosophy.
relevance_to_phd: Context for standards and governance of measurement.

name: First Telegraph Message
description: First telegraph message sent by Samuel Morse; launch of telecommunications era.
relevance_to_phd: Precedent for satellite data transmission.

name: ENIAC Unveiled
description: Demonstration of ENIAC, first general-purpose electronic computer.
relevance_to_phd: Grounds computational processing in data infrastructures.
